high_expertise.title: High expertise
high_expertise.label: VIS publication trend researcher
high_expertise.description: A visualization researcher examining structural change in the IEEE VIS publication corpus from 1990 through 2024. They are here to assess whether growth, venue mix, publication format, and collaboration signals point to durable shifts in the record.
high_expertise.expectations: They expect longitudinal, normalized comparisons using counts and shares, explicit derived measures, and enough granularity to inspect transitions and anomalies rather than just headline totals.

questions.text: How have the yearly publication counts and venue shares changed across the IEEE VIS record?
questions.answerable_because: Each row represents one year and conference, with paper counts, the full yearly total, and within-year share, so one chart can show both volume and venue-mix change over time.

questions.text: When did the publication record shift from conference papers toward journal papers?
questions.answerable_because: The table groups all papers by year and publication type, with counts and within-year shares, allowing a single time-series or stacked chart to show the transition among paper types.

questions.text: Did collaboration size and keyword coverage rise alongside the publication-format shift?
questions.answerable_because: The table provides yearly averages for authors per paper and yearly keyword availability measures derived from semicolon-delimited author and keyword fields, so one chart can compare these longitudinal signals against the same time axis.

low_expertise.title: Low expertise
low_expertise.label: Curious VIS newcomer
low_expertise.description: A general reader who wants an approachable overview of how IEEE VIS publishing has changed since 1990. They want to see the main growth story, the changing kinds of papers, and what became more common in recent records.
low_expertise.expectations: They expect plain-language questions, named conferences, simple time patterns, and one clear idea per chart without publication-data jargon.

questions.text: How many papers were published each year?
questions.answerable_because: This table has one row for each year with the total number of papers, so a single line or bar chart can show annual publishing volume from 1990 through 2024.

questions.text: Which conference contributed the most papers overall?
questions.answerable_because: This table counts all papers by named conference across the full dataset, allowing one ranked chart to identify the largest contributor.

questions.text: When did journal papers become the main kind of paper?
questions.answerable_because: The table records paper counts and yearly shares for each publication type, so a chart can show the point at which journal papers overtake other types or dominate the year.
